title: Smooth translation primitives from all cyclic residue maps
statement: Let G be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group with an element tau whose integral powers are dense. Suppose for each positive integer n a continuous homomorphism G→Multiplicative(ZMod n) sends tau to 1 (in additive notation). Let ell>1 be an integer and A an abelian group. For every function f:G→A with open right-translation stabilizer and ell*f(x)=0 for every x, there is a function h:G→A with open right-translation stabilizer and h(x*tau)-h(x)=f(x) for every x. Smooth means having open right stabilizer as in the discrete-module coinduction construction [def-exc-continuous-cohomology].

source.place: Finite modules paragraph: refining a cyclic quotient by the coefficient exponent; explicit finite summation implementation of this argument

proof.text: For the open right stabilizer of f choose an open normal subgroup U contained in it, using the compact totally disconnected group open-normal neighborhood basis. The finite quotient Q=G/U contains the image of tau, of positive order n. Put N=n*ell>1. The residue homomorphism q:G→Z/N sends tau to 1. Since 1 generates Z/N and n divides N, the homomorphism a:Z/N→Q sending 1 to the image of tau exists. The continuous homomorphisms a∘q and G→Q agree on every integral power of tau and hence agree on G by density and the Hausdorff topology of finite Q. Thus f is constant on fibers of q.

proof.text: Write F(i)=f(tau^i). Translation by tau^n lies in U, so F(n*m+i)=F(i) for all natural m,i. Split the sum over N terms into ell blocks of n terms. It equals ell times the sum over n terms, which is zero because ell kills each value of f. This also works when n=1.

source.place: Finite modules paragraph: refining a cyclic quotient by the coefficient exponent; explicit finite summation implementation of this argument

proof.text: Let idx(x) be the least nonnegative representative of q(x), and set h(x)=sum_{i<idx(x)}F(i). The kernel of q is open and fixes h under right translation, so h is smooth. The residue of x*tau increments idx(x) modulo N. Away from wraparound, the difference h(x*tau)-h(x) is F(idx(x))=f(x). At wraparound the vanishing sum over all N terms gives the same equality. These arguments also cover zero coefficients and f=0.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_primitive_of_cyclic_residues
    {G : Type u} [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G]
    [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]
    (τ : G) (hd : DenseRange (zpowersHom G τ))
    (residue : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → G →ₜ* Multiplicative (ZMod n))
    (hresidue : ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n),
      residue n hn τ = Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)
    (ell : ℕ) (hell : 1 < ell)
    {A : Type v} [AddCommGroup A] (f : G → A)
    (hf : IsOpen (rightStab G f : Set G)) (hkill : ∀ x, ell • f x = 0) :
    ∃ h : G → A, IsOpen (rightStab G h : Set G) ∧ ∀ x, h (x * τ) - h x = f x
